what: the upstream watcher's pure half — tree diffing and issue rendering
note: The first case file to use `runner: node`. The watcher's logic is a .mjs
under tool/, so `flutter test` cannot see it at all — and a suite the
gate cannot reach is exactly where an unkilled mutant would sit forever.
Group A is the diff itself: the four outcomes a watcher can report, plus
the two that only exist because git says so (a tree moving with no blob
moving; a tree SHA that disagrees with its own file list).
Group B is the rendered issue. B-4 is the one worth reading: swapping the
compare link from commits back to trees produces a link that is a 404 on
github.com — measured, not assumed — while every other assertion about
the body still passes. It is the shape of defect this whole harness
exists for: satisfiable, plausible, and dead.

cases.name: first run reports the baseline as additions
cases.to: if (prev === null) prev = { ref: next.ref, commit: next.commit, tree: '', files: {} };

cases.name: the tree/file-list consistency check is skipped
a modified file is reported as an added one
cases.to: if (before === undefined || before !== sha) added.push({ path, sha });

cases.name: removals are never detected
cases.to: if (false && next.files[path] === undefined) removed.push({ path, sha });

cases.name: paths come back in object order instead of sorted
a moved ref is not a change
cases.from: const refMoved = prev.ref === next.ref ? null : { from: prev.ref, to: next.ref };

cases.name: a tree that moved with no blob moving is silently unchanged
an issue can be rendered for a non-change
empty sections are rendered with their headings
the compare link is built from trees, which is a 404
